units.function: Exposes deterministic local SSH environment-fixture lifecycle commands: up, status, down and doctor. It resolves an instance-scoped state path, delegates SSH prerequisite/process/state/config work to adapter-utils, and prints human or JSON projections including host, port, user, workspace, logs, state and key/known-host paths.
units.dependencyDirection: env-lab CLI -> instance home/path helpers and @paperclipai/adapter-utils/ssh -> local filesystem, sshd/process/network fixture. The command is a thin presentation/orchestration layer; SSH trust, key generation, process isolation, cleanup and environment configuration ownership remain in the separately audited adapter-utils unit.
units.keyDataModels: instance ID/root; ssh-fixture/state.json; SSH support{supported,reason}; fixture status{running,state}; state host/port/username/workspaceDir/sshdLogPath/clientPrivateKeyPath/knownHostsPath; generated Environment config.
units.lifecycle: Resolve instance-scoped state -> up starts an SSH fixture and builds Environment config; status reads state and probes running state; doctor checks prerequisites plus state and reports key paths; down stops the recorded fixture. JSON mode serializes complete state/environment projections.
units.testAssessment: The already completed application:cli/__tests__/env-lab assessment was reused without rereading source: focused Vitest passed 2/2 and proves path shape plus absent-state projection only. SSH trust, credential permissions, process/network isolation, commands/files, cleanup/recovery and adversarial instance IDs are absent. CLI TypeScript checking passes.
units.designRationale: A deterministic disposable environment makes remote-execution adapters testable without production hosts or paid services. Instance-scoped state supports parallel local installations, and explicit status/doctor/down commands improve recovery from orphaned processes.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs vendor-neutral Connector and local-execution conformance labs that simulate capability declaration, task input, progress/events, approval pause/resume, evidence/result, cancellation, timeout, idempotency and runtime attestation without touching real enterprise systems or credentials.
units.companyOsFit: Use the fixture-lifecycle idea, then generalize it behind a ConnectorConformanceLab with deterministic scenarios and isolated ephemeral credentials. Fixture state must be clearly labeled non-production, resource-bounded, automatically cleaned and incapable of being confused with a real Agent or enterprise node.
units.responsibilityConflict: The SSH fixture is infrastructure test state rather than business work and carries no human/Agent responsibility record. That is acceptable only if it remains isolated from production projections and cannot generate evidence represented as real execution.

units.securityFindings: JSON/human output exposes local host/user/workspace/log/state/private-key-path/known-hosts topology and may expose additional Environment config fields; downstream logs must classify and redact it. Instance-ID containment, state-file permissions, private-key mode, port binding, host-key pinning, child-process ownership, PID reuse, symlink safety and cleanup after crashes are delegated and unproven here. down has no confirmation but targets a local test fixture. Command handlers do not add timeouts or error recovery; start/stop idempotency and orphan cleanup depend entirely on adapter-utils.
